analysis: This PR changes documentation only: docs/provider/installation.md (new 'Roll back to the previous release' section, head lines 219-256, plus the date bump at line 3) and docs/provider/troubleshooting.md (date bump, extended quarantine row at line 151, new regression row at line 152). No code, endpoints, or configs change, so no security control is altered directly. The docs describe a `darkbloom update --rollback` feature that restores a locally kept signed predecessor under ~/.darkbloom/recovery/predecessor/ and quarantines the replaced release. Relevant threats are T-043 (the watchdog and rollback authority is the same replaceable binary), T-013, T-034, and the update integrity chain, plus T-047 for the fan-helper note. The docs say the predecessor is a 'signed release' and that the swap is journaled and requires confirmation. They do not state that the predecessor's code signature and hashes are re-verified on rollback, or how a rollback to an older release interacts with coordinator minimum-version or revocation and App Attest qualification (T-054). The coordinator is expected to reject unqualified or revoked builds on reconnect. A rolled-back build that was later revoked would lose authorization rather than gain it, but the implementation is not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot confirm a downgrade-protection gap. The PR text also removes nothing from the existing hash and codesign verification description. One oddity: head lines 30-42 in installation.md look truncated or garbled. The 'Run the installer' step now shows TOML config where a bash code block was expected. That is a docs defect, not a security regression, though it could mislead operators about the installer invocation. Next-pass questions: does the rollback code verify the predecessor signature, the designated requirement, and the hashes before swapping; is the recovery/predecessor directory owner-only and protected from tampering by same-UID processes; and how does a rollback interact with revocation and qualification generations? Whether the threat model needs a T-043 or T-054 note about the predecessor snapshot cannot be determined from this docs-only diff.
